narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Foodie App Design"**

Foodie is one app with three front doors (customer, restaurant, delivery) and one visual language. Every screen is a quiet off-white page holding plain white cards with hairline borders, set in Nunito. Brand red is the only loud colour. It marks the one thing on a screen that matters most: the headline number, the primary action, the selected tab. Everything else is ink, muted ink and hairlines.

The system is flat and dense. People use these screens between tasks: a courier at a red light, a cook between tickets, a hungry customer. So hierarchy comes from type weight and a single red element, not from decoration. Screens start directly with a large page title. There is no coloured app bar.

The restaurant and delivery apps are the reference implementation. The customer app still uses an older navy/blue palette (`customer*` tokens in `constants/theme.ts`) and is migrating to this system screen by screen.
keyCharacteristics: Off-white page, white bordered cards, no shadows on content.
Nunito everywhere: Black for titles and numbers, Bold for labels and actions, Regular for body.
Brand red appears once or twice per screen, never as decoration.
Order status is always a tinted badge in the shared status colours.
Light and dark mode come from the same tokens via `useAppThemeColors()`.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Brand red fills at most one dominant element per screen (the hero card *or* a primary button group) plus the active tab and switches. If two red blocks compete, one of them becomes an outline button.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Screens never hard-code hex values. Read colours from `useAppThemeColors()` (`c.text`, `c.muted`, `c.card`, `c.border`, `c.screenBackground`, `c.brand`, `c.primary`) and status hues from `ORDER_STATUS_COLORS`. `#fff` on brand red is the one allowed literal.

rules.name: The Fill-vs-Text Red Rule
rules.body: Use `c.brand` for backgrounds, `c.primary` for red text, icons and links. Never put `c.brand` text on a dark surface.

rules.name: The Family-Not-Weight Rule
rules.body: Set weight by choosing a Nunito family (`Fonts.brand`, `Fonts.brandBold`, `Fonts.brandBlack`), never with `fontWeight`. A `fontWeight` on a Nunito family falls back to the system font on Android.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every currency value or count that can change uses `fontVariant: ['tabular-nums']`.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Content surfaces are separated by a hairline border, never a shadow. Shadows are reserved for things that float above the page: bottom sheets, modals and floating action buttons.

rules.name: The No-Nesting Rule
rules.body: A card never sits inside another card. Inside a card, group with hairline dividers or a Counter-filled inset.

dos: **Do** start every tab screen with the 28px Nunito Black page title on the counter background.
**Do** read every colour from `useAppThemeColors()` and every status colour from `ORDER_STATUS_COLORS`.
**Do** use the shared components (`Switch`, `Loader`, `DeliverySegmentedTabs`, `DeliveryStatTile`, `DeliveryEmptyState`, `RecentReviewsSection`) before writing new ones.
**Do** show real data only: when a number isn't available, show "—", "New" or an empty state.
**Do** give every loading, empty, error and busy state a designed treatment.
**Do** add `accessibilityRole` and a spoken label to every custom pressable.
donts: **Don't** add coloured app bars or navy headers; the old delivery `DeliveryHeader` was removed for this reason.
**Don't** use the `customer*` tokens (`customerBodyBg`, `customerNeutral`, `customerTextPrimary`…) in new work. They are legacy and being migrated away.
**Don't** put shadows on cards, tiles or list rows.
**Don't** nest cards, or add a coloured left/right accent stripe to a card.
**Don't** use emoji as icons; use Ionicons outline.
**Don't** ship placeholder numbers, fake trends ("+12%"), mock maps or buttons that do nothing.
**Don't** set `fontWeight` on text; pick the Nunito family instead.
